chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a virgin slave-girl without fully opening her; is ghusl (ritual bath) obligatory upon her? He said: “When the circumcised part is placed upon the circumcised part, then ghusl becomes obligatory, whether she is a virgin or not a virgin.”

key_terms.الْجَارِيَةَ: a slave-girl; here, the female subject of the legal question
key_terms.الْخِتَانُ: the circumcised part; used juridically to indicate sexual contact establishing ghusl
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ghusl (ritual bath) made obligatory after janabah
key_terms.يُفْضِي: to fully open or penetrate completely in this context

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory in sexual intercourse according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on janabah and the obligation of ghusl (ritual bath). It states that ghusl becomes obligatory upon the occurrence of sexual contact marked by the meeting of the circumcised parts, regardless of whether the woman is a virgin or previously married.
